profile.campus: Stream San Antonio, TX (second campus, SATA)
profile.address: 9550 Westover Hills Boulevard, San Antonio, TX 78251
profile.reading: Stream San Antonio II sits at 9550 Westover Hills Boulevard in Bexar County, Texas, internally coded SATA by the operator and described on Stream own site as the company second campus in the San Antonio market. Per that page, the facility carries 10.8 megawatts of total capacity, with 800 kilowatts immediately available, across 75,840 square feet, and is currently listed as available and being actively marketed for lease rather than fully occupied. No opening date or named tenant is disclosed for the facility. Stream Data Centers was founded in 1999 in Dallas, Texas, originally as a technical real estate affiliate of Stream Realty Partners, a larger commercial real estate firm. Ownership has changed more recently: Apollo-managed funds announced acquisition of a majority stake in Stream in August 2025 and completed the deal in November 2025, with Principal Asset Management taking a minority stake and Stream management retaining a minority position, and Stream now describes itself as a key operating platform within the Apollo ecosystem. The company markets its wholesale, powered-shell, and build-to-suit data center model, claiming more than 90 percent of its capacity leased to Fortune 100 customers and describing a pipeline exceeding four gigawatts with more than 27 delivered developments across markets including Dallas-Fort Worth, Phoenix, Chicago, San Antonio, and Atlanta, with a historical presence in Austin, Santa Clara, Denver, Minneapolis, and the Washington DC area. Westover Hills sits on the west side of San Antonio, a market that has grown steadily as a lower-cost alternative to Austin and Dallas for enterprise and cloud tenants seeking Texas-based capacity, and Stream description of this as its second San Antonio campus indicates the company saw enough sustained demand in the market to justify expanding beyond its original site there.

reading.body:
Stream San Antonio II is located in Bexar County on the grounds of a named address in San Antonio but publishes no power specification, total rack count, or IT load figure. Without disclosed capacity metrics, this campus cannot be ranked among Texas facilities by size or positioned in the operator's own portfolio of more than 20 active campuses. The operator is majority-owned as of November 2025 by Apollo Global Management and operates an active development pipeline of 4+ gigawatts across multiple markets, with more than 90 percent of existing capacity reportedly leased to Fortune 100 customers.

Stream maintains at least three campuses in the San Antonio market, per operator and trade press sources. This specific facility's role in that multi-campus strategy, its construction phase, and its target operational date are not published. Texas has 133 mapped data center facilities overall, of which only 18 publish power specifications totaling 468 megawatts, so published capacity data remains sparse in the state relative to mapped sites.

No certifications, power purchase agreements, interconnection queue status, or grid constraints for this location are published. Without capacity disclosure, this campus contributes no measurable data point to the state's published supply and cannot be assessed for its contribution to AI infrastructure scaling.
